chapter: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
title: The family plantation and sharecroppers
summary: Their father farmed a big place called Horace Grove, with sharecroppers on the other houses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you hear many of Louis Russell's records? I'll 'Case oh Down', I'm telling you, tell you one of my favorites. (SEVERAL VOICES AT ONCE) (GENERAL that record, I don't know ... CONVERSATION - EK TALKS ABOUT FARM AND JCH TALKS ABOUT RECORDS)
..... He had people working with him. There was 3 other houses on the plantation and they were sharecroppers. My father furnished everything and what they made, they gave him half.
How did your father get to acquire this much farm?

I really don't know. That was before my time, because I was quite small, but I do know that he was the first colored man that moved into this ... and after he moved in there these other people came, in small houses. The big house set way down in a grove. It was called Horace Grove and this big house set down
in the grove and the other houses set on the side.
Seems like a lot of property for a black man to own at that time. That's why I asked how -
Yes, it was about the biggest farm down there.
